issues.description: The problem statement's UML and description specify Stock.take(String): int, but the template implementation of Stock.take returns boolean. The solution implementation uses an int return (with -1 indicating failure). This mismatch in return type will cause students to face compilation or behavioral inconsistencies when they implement SealSaloon (which expects Stock.take to return an int) and follow the UML. Because the template's Stock is intended to be changed per the task, the differing signature is a structural inconsistency between the problem/spec and the provided starter code that can block students.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Stock.take signature with the UML and the solution by changing its return type from boolean to int. Update the method to return -1 when the ingredient is missing or insufficient and return the remaining quantity when successful (as in the solution). Ensure any code examples and instructions reference the int-based behavior.

issues.description: Return-type/signature mismatch for Stock.take: the Problem Statement (UML) and the Solution implement Stock.take(String) returning int (using -1 as a failure sentinel), but the Template's Stock.take(String) returns boolean. This inconsistency will confuse students implementing SealSaloon.checkOrderReady (which in the spec expects numeric return values to detect failure) and can lead to incorrect implementations or wasted time reconciling the mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Template's Stock.take(String) signature and implementation to return int (like the UML and Solution). Implement it to return -1 when the ingredient is missing or quantity is insufficient, and return the remaining quantity (or updated quantity) when successful. Update any usages accordingly (e.g., SealSaloon.checkOrderReady) so they compare against -1 to detect failure.
